about: NZ party placements on the compass axes from (a) published expert/manifesto/voter-survey data, each kept on its original scale with a stated rescaling to -10..+10, and (b) our own coding of each party's answers to the 36 compass items from its 2026 policy documents, recorded votes and leader statements (null = no evidence, never guessed). Scores in coded.axes use the same formula as the user test (data/guide/compass.json scoring). See guide/compass-method.md.
axes_scale: -10..+10 on every axis; economic: left (-) to right (+); social: GAL/libertarian (-) to TAN/authoritarian (+); populism: pluralist (-) to populist (+). "general_left_right" values are voters' or experts' overall left-right placements and are NOT the economic axis.
coding_scale: -2 strongly disagree / very negative .. +2 strongly agree / very positive relative to the item text; confidence high | medium | low; null = no public evidence found.

published_sources.name: Global Party Survey 2019 (expert survey)
published_sources.citation: Norris, Pippa (2020). Global Party Survey, 2019, V2.1 (party-level file, April 2020). Harvard Dataverse, doi:10.7910/DVN/WMGTNS.
published_sources.coverage_note: Five NZ parties were rated (12 experts each). The Māori Party and TOP were not included.

scales.V4_Scale: 0 = extreme economic left ... 10 = extreme economic right (government role in economy: privatisation, taxes, regulation, spending, welfare)
scales.V6_Scale: 0 = very liberal ... 10 = very conservative social values (personal freedoms, abortion, same-sex marriage, democratic participation vs order, tradition, stability)
scales.V8_Scale: 0 = strongly favours pluralist rhetoric ... 10 = strongly favours populist rhetoric
scales.V9: 0 = no importance ... 10 = great importance of populist rhetoric
scales.V11: 0 = favours increased public spending ... 10 = favours reduced taxation
scales.V13: 0 = strongly favours nationalism ... 10 = strongly favours multilateralism
scales.V16: 0 = strongly respects liberal-democratic norms ... 10 = strongly undermines them
scales.WVS_LR_PartyVoter: mean 1-10 left-right self-placement of the party's own voters in the World Values Survey (GPS auxiliary variable)

Marquardt, Michael Bernhard, Holger Döring, Allen Hicken, Melis Laebens, Juraj Medzihorsky, Anja Neundorf, Ora John Reuter, Saskia Ruth-Lovell, Keith R. published_sources.coverage_note: NZ is coded for elections up to 2017 only; ACT is coded only to 2002, and the Māori Party, TOP, Mana and later minor parties are not coded. Values for 2014 and 2017 are shown (earlier years are in the raw extract).

scales.v2pariglef: Economic left-right, measurement-model interval scale (lower = left). The _osp version is the ordinal original scale: 0 far-left ... 3 centre ... 6 far-right.
scales.v2pawelf_osp: Welfare: 0 strongly opposes ... 4 strongly supports welfare-state policies
scales.v2paculsup_osp: Cultural superiority: 0 strongly promotes superiority of a group/nation ... 4 strongly opposes
scales.v2paplur_osp: Political pluralism: 0 rejects ... 4 strongly embraces pluralism (respects opponents and institutions)
scales.v2palgbt_osp: LGBT social equality: 0 strongly opposes ... 4 strongly supports
scales.v2parelig_osp: Religious principles: 0 strongly promotes religious principles in politics ... 4 strongly opposes

rescale_formula.social: not rescaled: V-Party has no single GAL-TAN scale; the LGBT, religion, immigration and cultural-superiority items are shown separately

published_sources.name: CSES Module 5: collaborator (expert) left-right placements and respondent placements, New Zealand 2017 and 2020
published_sources.citation: The Comparative Study of Electoral Systems (www.cses.org). CSES MODULE 5 FULL RELEASE [dataset and documentation]. July 7, 2023 version. doi:10.7804/cses.module5.2023-07-07. New Zealand studies: NZES 2017 and NZES 2020 (collaborators Jack Vowles et al.).
published_sources.licence: Free for research use with citation (CSES data-download terms). Expert placement E5018 is the single judgment of the national collaborator team, not a multi-expert survey.

scales.E5018: 00 = Left ... 10 = Right, in the expert judgment of the CSES collaborator
scales.E3019: respondents' placement of each party, 0 = Left ... 10 = Right (means here are unweighted)

rescale_formula.general_left_right: (x - 5) * 2; this is a GENERAL left-right scale, not the economic axis, and is plotted on the economic axis only as a labelled approximation

published_sources.name: New Zealand Election Study 2020 and 2023: voters' mean placement of parties on a 0-10 left-right scale
published_sources.citation: Vowles, J. et al. New Zealand Election Study 2020 and 2023, weighted frequency tables (Sections B/C), hosted at jackvowles.com; question B5 (2023) / B7 (2020): "Where would you place these political parties on a scale from 0 to 10, where 0 means the most left and 10 means the most right?"
published_sources.licence: Public frequency tables; means and SDs computed here from the published weighted frequencies (excluding Don't know). Unit-record NZES data are subject to the NZES Data Usage Terms and were not used.

rescale_formula.general_left_right: (mean - 5) * 2; a GENERAL left-right scale as perceived by voters, shown alongside (not as) the economic axis

published_sources.name: ParlGov party table (development version, 2026 snapshot)
published_sources.citation: Döring, Holger and Philip Manow. Parliaments and governments database (ParlGov): Information on parties, elections and cabinets in established democracies. view_party.csv (development version, retrieved 23 Oct 2026).
published_sources.licence: ParlGov releases are published on Harvard Dataverse under CC0 1.0 (2024 release, doi:10.7910/DVN/2VZ5ZC).
published_sources.coverage_note: left_right / state_market / liberty_authority are ParlGov composites of the Castles-Mair (1984), Huber-Inglehart (1995) and Benoit-Laver (2006) expert surveys where a party was rated; parties with no expert rating (e.g. TOP, Conservative, New Conservative) carry the mean of their party family and are flagged based_on_expert_surveys=false. The most recent expert input is 2003-04 (Benoit-Laver), so these are historical.

not_retrieved.name: Manifesto Project (MARPOR / CMP) RILE scores for NZ manifestos
not_retrieved.reason: The Manifesto Project Main Dataset (MPDS2024a) and its API require a free registered account and API key; the download could not be completed from this research environment and no published table of NZ RILE scores for 2017-2023 was found. The dataset covers NZ parties (CMP ids 64110 Green, 64320 Labour, 64420 ACT, 64620 National, 64621 NZ First, 64901 Māori Party per the CSES Module 5 codebook). RILE = share of right-coded quasi-sentences minus share of left-coded ones (-100..+100).
not_retrieved.proposed_rescale: economic approximation: RILE / 10 (so -100..+100 -> -10..+10); note RILE mixes economic and social categories.

not_retrieved.name: Vote Compass New Zealand 2023 / 2026 (Vox Pop Labs for 1News/TVNZ) party positions
not_retrieved.reason: Vote Compass places parties on a two-dimensional (economic x social) chart inside the application, from party answers to 30 propositions calibrated by the Vox Pop Labs team with NZ political scientists; the party coordinates are shown to users but are not published as numbers in 1News articles or in a dataset. 1News articles on 10 Oct 2023 and 22 Oct 2026 publish electorate-level scores only.

not_retrieved.name: Chapel Hill Expert Survey
not_retrieved.reason: CHES covers European parties only; New Zealand is not included in any CHES wave.

soc_secs_traditional_marriage.evidence: MPs split on same-sex marriage (2013 conscience vote).

econ_cses_reduce_differences.evidence: 28% capital gains tax on investment property with "every dollar raised" going to health.

econ_nzes_privatisation.evidence: Future Fund locks assets in public ownership "instead of selling off our assets and opening the gates to foreign investors".

econ_nzes_big_business.evidence: "crack down on big companies who charge excessive prices"; "the big companies can't rip you off".

econ_secs_limited_government.evidence: Future Fund, Medicard and fare caps expand the state's role, while promising "not a new layer of bureaucracy".

econ_secs_business.evidence: "Small Business First" package; "leveling the playing field for Kiwi businesses and innovation".

soc_vsa_gods_laws.evidence: Took abortion out of the Crimes Act in government (2020); Rainbow Pae Ora strategy.

soc_vsa_not_tougher.evidence: Voted against reinstating three strikes; would end youth boot camps; but would "crack down" on price gouging.

soc_secs_abortion.evidence: Government bill that decriminalised abortion (2020); most Labour MPs voted for it on a conscience vote.

soc_secs_traditional_marriage.evidence: Marriage equality was Labour MP Louisa Wall's bill (2013), supported by most Labour MPs.

soc_secs_military.evidence: Hipkins rejected US calls to lift spending to a set level: "no other country should dictate New Zealand's military spend"; would not join AUKUS.

soc_ess_gay_free.evidence: Rainbow Pae Ora health strategy; passed the conversion-practices ban (2022).

soc_cses_immigrants_economy.evidence: "Migrants bring much-needed energy and skills"; immigration "planned around what New Zealand needs".

pop_cses_majority.evidence: Opposed the Treaty Principles Bill; opposed Māori-ward referendums.

nzes2023_voters_general_left_right.note: voters' general left-right placement, not an economic-only scale

econ_nzes_big_business.evidence: Supermarkets "making $1 million a day in excessive profits"; large corporations "profiting from the public without contributing back".

econ_secs_business.evidence: Keeps 28% rate for SMEs but 33% for the largest corporates and would "Regulate businesses ... to be socially and environmentally responsible".

econ_secs_fiscal_responsibility.evidence: "Enabling greater government borrowing for investing in infrastructure; Avoiding arbitrary limits on government debt and expenditure".

econ_secs_gun_ownership.evidence: "continuing to oppose possession of military-style semi-automatic firearms"; robust licensing and registration.

soc_vsa_gods_laws.evidence: Reproductive rights, rainbow and drug-law reform; opposes any religious basis for law.

soc_vsa_not_tougher.evidence: Prioritise rehabilitation; voted against reinstating three strikes; repeal the Misuse of Drugs Act.

soc_vsa_crack_down.evidence: Rehabilitation over punishment; end military-style academies; raise the age of criminal responsibility.

soc_ess_gay_free.evidence: Rainbow communities manifesto; increase resourcing for rainbow organisations.

soc_cses_immigrants_economy.evidence: New residency pathways; refugee quota to 5,000; migrant workers "contribute to Business success".

soc_cses_culture_harmed.evidence: Communities of Colour policy; "Welcoming, safe and fair pathways to make Aotearoa home".

pop_cses_people_decide.evidence: Citizens' assemblies for local decisions, but entrench the Māori seats beyond referendums.

pop_cses_rich_powerful.evidence: Lobbying and donation reform so "big money and professional lobbying can have less influence over politics".

nzes2023_voters_general_left_right.note: voters' general left-right placement, not an economic-only scale

econ_wvs_incomes.evidence: Fiscal plan aims at "much lower, flatter taxes"; no capital gains tax; opposes wealth taxes.

econ_wvs_ownership.evidence: Open power transmission to private investment; opposes break-ups and state-run alternatives; public-private partnerships for cancer centres.

econ_nzes_big_business.evidence: Criticises "political leadership blame[ing] companies for their prices", which "creates greater bureaucracy".
